summary: Embedding payload protocol mismatch causing intermittent rerank top-k variance and latency spikes
description:
Issue summary: AtlasSearch reports intermittent changes in rerank top-k ordering and 200-500ms spikes in per-request latency for their dedicated pool. Behavior started after a client-side SDK update two days ago.

Impact: Approximately 5-8% of requests for a high-volume rerank route return different top-10 ordering compared to historical baseline; customers notice relevance regressions and occasional 5xx retries. Latency spikes correlate with requests that include small payloads (~64 vectors) versus larger batches.

Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated), prod us-east, service route rerank-v1 pinned to open-rerank-1.1. Ingest pipeline uses SDK-js v2.4.0 on the customer side.

Observed on 2026-03-09 16:34:12 UTC and recurring.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer sends batched embeddings (payloads of variable shape) via POST /v1/embeddings with header 'Embed-Format: binary_npy' and Content-Type application/octet-stream.
2) Immediately issue rerank call using returned embedding IDs to /v1/rerank with same client.
3) Observe top-k ordering differences compared to a cached baseline response run against same inputs in staging.
4) Re-run with identical inputs but using SDK-js v2.3.1 (previous version) — behavior appears stable.

Note: The customer provided a small repro bundle in S3 referenced in attachments.
logs:
Sample log excerpt (redacted):
[2026-03-09T16:34:12Z] ingest: recv payload id=abc123 len=8192 proto=proto_v1 header=(embed-dtype=float32, order=fortran)
[2026-03-09T16:34:12Z] serving-runtime: batch 47 reorder detected: incoming-order != preferred-order -> queued reorder (batch-id=47)
[2026-03-09T16:34:12Z] rerank-service: compute topk for request req=xyz789 model=open-rerank-1.1 latency=372ms topk-hash=0x7f4a2 (previous=0x9c3d1)
Errors: occasional 'incompatible-dim: header mismatch' logged then fallback to compatibility-path (quant-cpu).
comments: Support - Aisha: Opened ticket after customer provided diffs showing ordering changes and latency outliers. Asked for complete SDK request traces and the S3 repro bundle.

Customer - AtlasSearch (Michael Li): Confirmed SDK upgrade to 2.4.0 coincides with first occurrence. We send embeddings as serialized numpy arrays from Python workers and as typed buffers from Node aggregation. Repro bundle uploaded to s3://atlassearch/repro/246119.zip

SRE - Marco Chen: Noted logs show 'order=fortran' in header for some batches; our serving runtime expects C-order numpy arrays by default. Hypothesis: mix of row-major vs column-major ordering + missing value for endian flag causing different memory views and subsequent quantization path changes.

Dev - Priya Nair: Found a code path in sdk-js v2.4.0 that sets Embed-Format header to 'binary_npy' but serializes as little-endian flatbuffers in the Node aggregator. Patch candidate: ensure header matches serialization protocol or coerce on ingest. Working on minimal fix PR.
Support - Aisha: Customer requested ETA for workaround; provided temporary guidance to pin to sdk-js v2.3.1 or to force explicit 'order=C' conversion on client side.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Client-side SDK change introduced a serialization / header mismatch (np.save vs Node buffer) causing serving-runtime to mis-detect layout; this triggers a compatibility fallback that uses CPU quantized path leading to numeric differences and higher latency.

Hypothesis B: Mixed endianness between Python-produced arrays and Node aggregator leads to byte-order misinterpretation; detected 'order=fortran' values are unexpected and correlate with altered topk hashes.
Repro status: Customer repro bundle reproduces ordering variance locally when replayed through prod ingest endpoint. Running packaged unit test against sdk-js v2.4.0 reproduces header mismatch.
Initial mitigation: Add stricter validation in embeddings-ingest to reject mismatched header+payload combinations with clear 400 to callers (prevents silent fallback).
Performance note: When fallback path triggers quant-cpu, CPU-bound rerank workload latency increases by ~200-350ms per request in our measurements for these payload sizes.
temporary_workaround: Advise customer to pin sdk-js to 2.3.1 or to explicitly serialize numpy arrays to C-order little-endian and set header 'Embed-Format: numpy_c_le'. We provided a small conversion snippet to run before send. Also recommended to add Content-Encoding: gzip to large payloads to reduce variant handling.
resolution_notes: In progress: engineering patch being prepared to validate embed payload header, auto-normalize common mismatches (coerce Fortran->C order, endian normalization) and emit clear telemetry when fallback occurs. Target hotfix PR to serving-runtime planned for 2026-03-13 and rollout to dedicated pools for affected customers by 2026-03-14. Post-fix will include metrics and an alert when fallback path triggers >0.5% of traffic.
next_steps: 1) Create PR to normalize legacy embed payloads (Dev Priya). 2) Add ingest validation rule and a short-circuit 400 with explicit error message (SRE Marco). 3) Coordinate hotfix rollout to AtlasSearch dedicated pool and run customer repro before and after. 4) Postmortem and SDK compatibility note in SDK release notes.
notes_for_records: Related to prior tickets SUP-91455 (embedding cache invalidation) and SUP-91357 (ingest normalization). This ticket emphasizes protocol compatibility rather than model math. Keep channel #support and #serving-runtime in loop.
